claim: The best published difficulty-proportional allocation rule captures half or more of the oracle gain over uniform allocation on workloads the model mostly solves, but at most 13% on hard workloads even when given true pass rates; on CodeContests with Llama-3-8B (mean p 0.021) IAS captures 1% and with Llama-3-70B (mean p 0.074) 2%.
stance_target: L3 budget-routing vs oracle is partly occupied for pass-rate signals
quoted_support: On public math, code and formal-proof samples, the best published difficulty-proportional rule captures half or more of the oracle gain on benchmarks the model mostly solves, but at most 13% on hard workloads, even given true pass rates.
numbers: CodeContests Llama-3-8B N=140 mean p 0.021 oracle gain +4.8 pts IAS 1%
CodeContests Llama-3-70B N=140 mean p 0.074 +6.0 pts IAS 2%

claim: With a verifier and a prior from a related model's past runs on the same inputs, Thompson Sampling raises the solved share on the hardest workload from 14% to 27%; without such a prior no tested policy beats round-robin, and the gain vanishes between prior rank correlations of about 0.3 and 0.55.
stance_target: information (prior quality), not policy, drives routing gain
scope_conditions: Sec 5; verifier required; novel inputs get no gain
quoted_support: With a verifier and a prior from a related model’s past runs on the same inputs, Thompson Sampling raises the solved share on the hardest workload from 14% to 27%; without such a prior, no policy we tested beats round-robin.

claim: Cheap priors (text regression, LLM-derived features, zero-shot LLM difficulty judgments, dissimilar-model history) correlate weakly with true pass rates and give no gain over round-robin (at most 1.7 points at 16 attempts per problem).
stance_target: a model-internal or verbal confidence prior must reach rank correlation above about 0.3-0.55 to help; verbal/probe confidence untested here
quoted_support: Text regressions, LLM-derived features and a dissimilar model’s history all correlate weakly with true pass rates and give no gain, and fresh proxy samples lose because their cost is charged.

claim: The gain requires a verifier whose false acceptance rate is well below the workload pass rate: it survives 20% false rejections but all but vanishes at a 5% false acceptance rate.
stance_target: verifier-quality dependency relevant to self-written tests (L4) and execution budgets (L3)
quoted_support: it survives 20% false rejections and charging attempts by length, but it all but vanishes at a 5% false acceptance rate

claim: A survey of 221 LLM allocation papers finds at least 13 (5.9%) give the hardest inputs the most attempts, with 4 more borderline; one surveyed rule samples until a confidence threshold is met so low-confidence inputs consume more samples.
scope_conditions: Sec 3; LLM-assisted coding, authors treat 13 as lower bound
quoted_support: Thirteen of the 221 papers (5.9%) meet this strict definition after an LLM-assisted, author-reviewed check of every candidate against its full text, and four more are borderline (17, or 7.7%).
